lessons.c: A PROGRAM is a POU whose variables keep their values between cycles. A task calls it every cycle. MAIN is the usual top-level program, and it can call other programs.
lessons.x: MAIN calls ConveyorControl and AlarmHandling each cycle.
lessons.ex: Split a sketch machine into two programs and decide what MAIN calls.
q: Splitting a machine into programs helps:
A program is a kind of:
POU covers programs, functions and function blocks.

lessons.c: A FUNCTION returns one value and has no memory, so the same inputs always give the same output. It is ideal for calculations such as scaling.
lessons.x: Convert a raw sensor count into millimetres.
lessons.ex: Write a function that converts Celsius to Fahrenheit.
q: Same inputs to a function give:

lessons.c: A FUNCTION_BLOCK has inputs, outputs and its own memory. You create instances of it, and each instance keeps its own data, like one object per motor.
lessons.x: FB_Motor gets three instances: one each for the three conveyor motors.
lessons.ex: Sketch the inputs and outputs of a FB_Valve block.
q: A copy of the block with its own data
FB_Motor reused for three motors means:
They need memory, so they are function blocks.
lessons.code:
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Motor
VAR_INPUT  bStart : BOOL; END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT bRunning : BOOL; END_VAR

bRunning := bStart;

lessons.c:
A GVL declares variables that are shared across the whole project, inside VAR_GLOBAL. You access them as GVL_Name.Variable.

Use them sparingly, for things like I/O and shared status.
lessons.x: GVL_IO holds every sensor and valve so any program can read them.
lessons.ex: Create a GVL_IO and move one input into it.
q: A GVL is a list of global variables.
You access a GVL variable by:
Use the list name, a dot, then the variable.

lessons.c: Group related data with STRUCT, name states with ENUM, and build libraries of function blocks. Reuse cuts bugs and makes new machines faster to build.
lessons.x: A ST_Motor struct holds start, running and fault flags in one tidy variable.
lessons.ex: Define a struct for a valve with open, closed and fault flags.
q: Enums give readable names to values.
